text: Umesh Reddy, born in 1969 in Basappa Malige, a village in Chitradurga district, Karnataka, is a serial killer and serial rapist from India. He confessed to killing 18 women and was convicted in 9 cases, with the police believing he raped at least 20 women across Karnataka, Maharashtra, and Gujarat, many of whose crimes went unreported due to fear of social stigma. After being selected for the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), Reddy was posted in Jammu and Kashmir, where he attempted to rape a commandant's daughter and fled to Chitradurga. In 1996, he joined the District Armed Reserve (DAR) Police, unaware of his CRPF background; a prior road rage incident was ignored by local authorities. He completed police training in Madhya Pradesh and returned to Karnataka. Reddy carefully targeted housewives between 11 am and 3 pm, gaining entry by claiming to need water or an address, then threatening them with a knife, forcing them to remove their clothes, tying them up, and raping them—often while they were unconscious or choked. After the rape, he killed the victims, stole their jewellery to make it appear as a robbery, and escaped with their undergarments, which were later found under his clothes during police arrests. In November 1996, he attempted to rape a high school girl in KEB Colony, who hit him and escaped; on 6 December 1996, he raped and murdered 16-year-old Roopa in the same area. The next month, he was arrested and dismissed from service when his first victim identified him at a Republic Day parade. He was charged with Roopa’s murder, later acquitted in 2004 due to insufficient evidence. A court ordered his transfer to Bellary jail, but in March 1997, he escaped during transfer and committed further crimes, including killing an income tax officer’s wife in Bangalore, a girl in Ahmedabad, two girls in Baroda, and a widow in Kunigal. He stole lingerie from backyards; on 7 July 1997, he was arrested in Peenya for stealing undergarments, with a gunny bag of lingerie recovered. He claimed his name was "Ramesh" at arrest and escaped within 24 hours during transfer to MICO Layout police station. His father filed a habeas corpus petition, leading to the suspension of two police officers and a lookout notice issued for Ramesh. On 28 February 1998, he raped and murdered 37-year-old widow Jayashree Maradi Subbaiah in Peenya, and the police believe he had sex with her body. When her 8-year-old son saw him, Reddy told the boy an evil spirit had entered his mother’s body and that he had tied her to a window grill, then fled claiming to go for a doctor. He attempted to rape another woman in Peenya, escaping by jumping from a first-floor window after spraining his ankle and being caught by neighbors. In 1999, he escaped again near Hirekerur and was arrested by inspector Nyame Gowda in Chikkaballapur. On 3–4 March 2002, he escaped again while being transferred from Bellary to Bangalore in a KSRTC bus; DAR personnel claimed he was handcuffed, but Reddy denied it and stated he bought rum and chicken to gain their trust. When the bus stopped at a dhaba near Hiriyur bypass, he requested to remove his handcuffs, then escaped into the fields. Over the next two months, he raped three girls in Davangere, Hubli-Dharwad, and Pune, stole three mobile phones and two credit cards, worked as a waiter in a Pune hotel, stole cash and clothes, and fled to Dharwad. On 17 May 2002, he arrived in Bangalore from Tumkur, left luggage in the Yeshwanthpur railway station cloakroom, and visited a salon for a haircut and shave. Auto-rickshaw driver Sathyavelu recognized him from a newspaper photo and a prior court appearance, called his brother Rajendran, and alerted the police. Sathyavelu kept watch outside the salon and tipped off the police when Reddy exited. Inspector Nagaraja Urs intercepted him near Sharief Nagar and arrested him. Initially denying his identity, Reddy admitted to being the serial killer after being taken to the station. The police rewarded Sathyavelu with ₹20,000. Reddy was found wearing a bra and panties; his baggage contained 18 pairs of panties, 10 bras, 8 churidars, 6 saris, 4 blouses, and 2 nighties. He was tried and convicted in 9 cases, including Jayashree Subbaiah’s rape, and acquitted in 11 cases due to insufficient evidence. On 26 October 2006, Judge K Sukanya of the Bengaluru fast-track court sentenced him to death, a 7-year sentence with a ₹25,000 fine, and a 10-year sentence with a ₹25,000 fine. Reddy sought mercy, claiming he wanted to study and care for his mother, but the judge refused. The death sentence was referred to the Karnataka High Court. On 4 October 2007, a division bench convicted Reddy, with Justice V G Sabhahit upholding the death penalty and Justice Ravi B Naik advocating life imprisonment without amnesty. A third judge, Justice S. R. Bannurmath, was appointed to resolve the tie. On 18 February 2009, Bannurmath upheld the death sentence, confirming it at the High Court level. On 1 February 2011, the Supreme Court upheld the death sentence, with Justices Altamas Kabir and A K Pathak stating Reddy was incapable of rehabilitation and that the rape and murder of Jayashree fell under the "rarest of the rare" category, a legal requirement for capital punishment. Reddy immediately filed a mercy petition before the President of India; on 7 May 2012, the Government of Karnataka rejected it, and on 12 May 2013, the President also rejected it. He filed a fresh petition, and on 4 November 2022, the Supreme Court commuted his death sentence to 30 years of imprisonment. A Kannada film, Umesh (2013), and another film, Khatarnak or Khataranak Umesh Reddy (2013), are fictionalized portrayals of his life. Adi Lokesh portrayed Reddy in Dandupalya 2 and Dandupalya 3 as one of the inmates of the Dandupalya gang in Hindalga Prison. A three-episode documentary titled Beast of Bangalore: Indian Predator, released on Netflix on 16 December 2022, depicts Reddy’s crimes and includes interviews with local police officials, victims, and associates who aided him.
